      "role": "user",
      "content": "What's the safest way to add a NOT NULL column to a 50M-row Postgres table without locking it?"
    }
  ],
  "output_text": "Add the column as nullable first, backfill in batches, then add the NOT NULL constraint as a NOT VALID check so existing rows aren't rewritten in one pass. Concretely:\n\n1. `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN col type` (nullable, no default) - this is instant, no table rewrite.\n2. Backfill in small batched UPDATEs (5-10k rows at a time) so you don't hold a long-running transaction or bloat WAL.\n3. Add `CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID`, which is instant.\n4. `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` in a separate transaction - this scans the table but only takes a lock that permits concurrent reads and writes.\n5. Once validated, promote the column to NOT NULL; on Postgres 12+ this is metadata-only since the CHECK constraint already guarantees it.\n\nAvoid a single `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN col type NOT NULL DEFAULT x` - on older Postgres that rewrites every row under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for the duration.",

  },
